explanation: A resistor converts electrical energy to heat at a rate P = IV, which (using V = IR) can be written P = I^2 R or P = V^2/R. Because power goes as the SQUARE of the current, doubling the current quadruples the power dissipated — the P-versus-I curve is a parabola opening upward, not a line. The form you choose on the AP exam depends on what is held fixed: at fixed current the larger resistor dissipates more (P = I^2 R), but at fixed voltage the SMALLER resistor dissipates more (P = V^2/R). The orange dot sweeps along the I^2 R parabola while the pink dot marks your chosen operating point, with the live readout giving P in watts.
bullets: Three equivalent forms: P = IV = I^2 R = V^2 / R.
P-vs-I is a parabola: double I quadruples the power.
Fixed current: bigger R dissipates more (P = I^2 R).
Fixed voltage: smaller R dissipates more (P = V^2 / R).
